messages.author: f1a99d231af89cb9
messages.subject: AX3 in Children
parts:
Dear Vincent, hi community 

I plan to use the Axivity 3 in my cohort of children and adolescents aged 6-16 years with obesity and a normalweight control group over a period of 14-21 days. What presettings/set up I may need to use to get validated results for this age group? Is the preset configuration that comes along in OMGUI / GGIR ok to use for children, i.e., can I trust the results on time spent in moderate/vigorous intensity or do I need adaption? Anything else  to consider for a study in children? Thank you very much!

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] AX3 in Children
parts:
Dear Christoph,

Whether you can "trust" GGIR depends on your understanding of what GGIR does, your ability to tailor GGIR to your study protocol and research needs, and the extent to which you account for all this when interpreting the results.

To help you with this we provide documentation on what GGIR can do with references to literature, we provide a list of possible cut-points that you may want to consider, we offer training courses on how to use GGIR, and I/we can provide support with specific questions/problems here in the google group or as paid consultancy.

In my opinion the term 'validated' is overrated in this field. Many of the 'gold standards' come with significant limitations themselves, and true 'validity' in the field heavily depends on how a method is used and interpreted. Methodological research is important to help understand a method and its limitations, but should not be seen as a certificate to justify unlimited use in research.

Best regards,

Vincent

Dr. Vincent van Hees | Independent consultant | https://accelting.com/

after a couple of weeks using ggir in children I have a question regarding the number of stepcounts: How dies ggir actually count a step? are there parameters to adjust for what impuls is counted as step? In my studies, individuals have very high step counts (10’000-25’000 per day). Inwish this to be true but I do not really trust these numbers. Is this a setting issue which can be adjusted?

messages.author: 017566be30afa7f3
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] AX3 in Children
parts:
Hi Chris,

I assume you have been using the Verisense step algorithm?

The step detection happens inside that algorithm which is called as an external function by GGIR, by which it is not part of GGIR.

So, for validity question you need to contact the author Matt Patterson who is also in this google group and may see your message. Further, some of your questions may be answered by:
  • https://github.com/ShimmerEngineering/Verisense-Toolbox/blob/master/Verisense_step_algorithm/validation_paper.pdf 
  • https://www.mdpi.com/1424-8220/22/24/9984 

Vincent
